ambiguities.description: Vendor identification is clear (vendor number), but tax ID is explicitly known to be non-unique due to duplicate vendor records and shared parent filings. Is there a plan to enforce tax ID uniqueness or merge duplicates, and should tax ID still be modeled as an attribute despite being unreliable?

source_references.excerpt: We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.
The duplicates are a real problem. There's a cleanup project that's been on the roadmap for two years.

ambiguities.description: Address is mentioned as having three variants (remit-to, ship-from, legal) that are 'frequently different and frequently wrong', but no structure or identification for these addresses was captured. Should each address type be modeled as a separate fact type/value type, and what is the internal structure (street, city, etc.)?

source_references.excerpt: Legal name. Tax ID. Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: 'Tier' is an overloaded term used by both Procurement (spend tier: bronze/silver/gold) and Compliance (risk tier: low/medium/high) for different concepts, causing confusion. This was resolved into two distinct fields, but the naming/UI disambiguation issue in daily use remains unresolved ('nobody says spend tier and risk tier').

source_references.excerpt: And you both call it "tier." -- We both call it tier and it causes genuine chaos.

ambiguities.description: The rule for post-suspension handling of in-flight purchase orders (e.g., a possible 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and deferred to a steering group/Legal. The model currently has no representation of this transitional state or rule.

source_references.excerpt: My position is that everything halts immediately. That's what suspension means. ... This goes to the sourcing steering group. It's a policy call, not a modeling call, and Legal has to be in the room.

ambiguities.description: The 'preferred vendor' flag mentioned by Mei (informal spreadsheet column indicating which vendor to prefer when multiple can supply the same item) is explicitly ad hoc and not modeled per stakeholder agreement, but flags a potential future fact type once/if criteria are formalized.

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." It means if two vendors can supply the same thing, buy from this one. It's not in the system anywhere. ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between RiskReview and Vendor being 'current' is stated as a business rule but it's unclear from the transcript whether 'current' is a boolean flag on the RiskReview record itself, a separate reference from Vendor to its current RiskReview, or derived from dates. The model assumes a separate fact type 'Vendor has current signed-off RiskReview' but the underlying implementation mechanism is not specified.

source_references.excerpt: A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.
Mei, does the system model it that way? -- The review is its own record.

ambiguities.description: Contact reference/identification: the transcript does not specify how an individual Contact record is identified (no contact ID or unique field mentioned) beyond name/email/phone. A reference_mode of 'contact_id' was assumed but not confirmed by stakeholders.

source_references.excerpt: Each vendor has one primary contact. Name, email, phone number.
A given vendor in a given region has exactly one primary contact.

ambiguities.description: Temporal tracking: vendor status, tier, and contact assignments appear to be current-state only (e.g., status transitions draft->active->suspended, contact changes per region). It's unclear whether history of these changes (e.g., prior contacts, prior statuses, prior tiers) needs to be tracked for audit purposes, especially given compliance's emphasis on audit trails for reviews.

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.
Since we went to regional sourcing last year, it's one primary contact per region.

ambiguities.description: Whether a vendor with zero risk reviews can still be 'suspended' vs only 'draft'/'active' is unclear -- the transcript establishes active requires a current signed-off review and draft has none, but doesn't clarify whether a suspended vendor must have (or retain) a review record.

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has a current signed-off review. A draft vendor has no review at all -- that's the normal case, that's what draft means.
